## ✨ Highlights

- 🔇 **The console's share, your call**: what a node's serial console gets of its services' output is a setting now - lower it, or turn it off, on a node whose serial port nobody reads. An emulated serial port costs CPU for every byte: with HAProxy logging every request, `init` took 2 % of an older core for it, and HAProxy serves 14 % more with the console's share off.
- 🖥️ **An image without a serial console**: a schematic may ask for the screen alone (`"console": "screen"`) - for nodes you install by hand and watch another way.

## ⚙️ Node

- **The services' share of the console** (`SystemService.ConsoleBudgetGet` / `ConsoleBudgetSet`): what the console gets of HAProxy's and the extensions' output - 2 KiB a second with a 64 KiB burst by default, the rest left out and said so - is kept per node on STATE (`config/console.json`) and applies at once: a lower share takes hold within a second. `0` keeps janusd's own log on the console and nothing of the services'; every line is still kept whole where it was (`janusctl system logs`, the LOGS partition, the log targets). Readers see it, admins change it; an event records each change.
  - `janusctl system console-budget` shows it; `-rate BYTES`, `-burst BYTES`, `-default` change it.
  - Two metrics: `janus_console_budget_bytes_per_second` (and `_burst_bytes`), `janus_console_lines_left_out_total{service}`.
  - 📖 [Log forwarding - the console](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/log-forwarding.md#the-console)
- **Why**: on a node logging every request, the budget is always full, and `init` - which relays it to the serial port, byte by byte through the hypervisor - took about 2 % of a 2013 Xeon core, 0.8 % of a single 2012 core, 0.4 % of a 2023 one: the same bytes on slower cores, not a change of Janus. Measured on the lab and on two production nodes; the console flood test now proves the share off: the console got 698 bytes in 10 s (janusd's notes), HAProxy's lines all in janusd's copy, and **60,803 requests/s against 53,164** with the default share.

## 🏭 Image factory

- **`"console": "screen"`** in a schematic: the image boots with `console=tty0` alone - the first boot's credentials and janusd's log on the screen, nothing on a serial port. Unset, `"serial"`, as before (the screen and the serial port); named, it is kept as written like a branch or a track: the default schematic's ID doesn't move. A release's catalog lists the choices it offers (`"console": ["serial", "screen"]`, from this release on); the builder at janus.sw-servers.net/builder shows the choice when the release has it. **The Controller's own machines never get it**: it reads their serial console to watch them register.
  - 📖 [Image factory - the console](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/image-factory.md#the-console)

## 🖥️ Controller

- A **Console** card in System › Services: the share in force, the lines left out, Apply / Turn off / Default - for those who may change the node.
- The builder's **Console** choice (above).

## 🧪 Tests and tooling

- `qemu-console-flood-test` sets the share to 0 under the same load and back: nothing of HAProxy on the console, everything in janusd's copy, then the default again.
- An image built from a `screen` schematic carries `console=tty0 panic=-1` and boots to HAProxy and the API with nothing on its serial port (the build box, OVMF/KVM); the default image still carries `console=tty0 console=ttyS0`.
- Measured and not kept: `init` writing to the serial tty device itself instead of `/dev/console` - the cost is the byte-by-byte round trip through the hypervisor, not the kernel's wait for the port.

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **Nodes**: the usual A/B update; the console's share is the same until set. A node that logs every request to its stdout and whose serial console nobody reads may set `janusctl system console-budget -rate 0`.
- **The Controller**: update it for the Console card; it works with nodes not yet updated (the card says the node's version lacks it).
- **janusctl**: the new command needs the updated nodes.
- **Schematics**: `"console": "screen"` builds for this release on; the image factory refuses it for an older one.
